# task-4f224c75: horizontal gap filling

Confirmed on one demo and one accepted test. In each row, locate repeated marker cells (in the demo they were 4 on background 9; in the accepted test they were 0 on background 3). For each pair of consecutive markers on that row, change the background cells strictly between them to color 2. Preserve the markers, all other cells, and grid dimensions. Do not extend beyond the outermost markers. Apply row-by-row; do not infer vertical filling.

## Evidence and variant
- Demo: rows containing color-4 markers had alternating 9 gaps; those gaps became 2. Rows without markers stayed all 9.
- Accepted test: marker/background palette was 0/3 rather than 4/9. All within-row background gaps between markers became 2; unrelated background remained 3.
- Another accepted test used markers 6 on background 3 in a 13×11 grid. It confirmed the same rule even with repeated rows and runs of different lengths: fill only the cells strictly between consecutive 6s on each row with 2; preserve markers and the rest of the grid.
- Current accepted test: marker 3 on background 8 in a 6×16 grid, including rows with marker sequences at different offsets and counts. Filled only the intervening cells (e.g., between columns 3 and 5, or a longer run between columns 7 and 13), preserving all 3s, all exterior 8s, and empty rows. Palette is instance-variable; output gap color remains 2.

## Additional confirmed variant
- Solved 14×15 instance with marker 6 on background 7. Rows contained alternating 6/7 sequences, including sequences of 2–7 markers at varying offsets. The correct output changed every 7 strictly between consecutive 6s on the same row to 2; all 6s, leading/trailing 7s, and rows without markers stayed unchanged. No vertical filling.

## Further confirmed instance
- Solved a 27×15 grid with marker 8 on background 9. The same row-wise rule held: replace only 9s strictly between consecutive 8s with 2; preserve leading/trailing 9s and all rows without markers. Rows had varying numbers and spacing of markers, including adjacent marker pairs with one-cell gaps.

## Further confirmed instance
- Solved a 10×13 grid with marker 5 on background 6. Apply the same rule: on each row, replace background 6 strictly between consecutive marker 5s with 2. Preserve leading/trailing 6s, all 5s, rows without a marker, and grid dimensions. This confirms the marker/background colors are instance-variable even when the marker pattern starts near the edge.

## Further confirmed instance
- Solved a 12×10 grid with marker 0 on background 5. On each row, replaced only 5s strictly between consecutive 0s with 2; preserved all leading/trailing 5s, marker cells, rows/cells without enclosed gaps, and dimensions. This reconfirms that marker and background are instance-variable (including marker 0) and output gap color stays 2.

## Further confirmed instance
- Solved an 11×23 test with marker 4 on background 3. Row-wise gaps strictly between consecutive 4s became 2, including alternating sequences of 4s across rows with 2–6 markers. All leading/trailing 3s, rows without markers, and dimensions were preserved. This is another confirmation of the palette-variable rule.
